stem: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following is the customer's responsibility when running an application on Amazon EC2?

choices.text: Patching the underlying EC2 hypervisor
Configuring the guest operating system and application-level security groups
Maintaining physical security of the data center
Decommissioning the underlying storage hardware

explanation: In the shared responsibility model, AWS manages security of the cloud (hardware, hypervisor, physical facilities), while the customer manages security in the cloud, including guest OS patching, security groups, and IAM. Options A, C, and D are AWS's responsibilities.

stem: A security team wants to add an extra layer of protection so that a compromised password alone cannot be used to access the AWS root user. Which control should they enable?

choices.text: AWS Config rules
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user
VPC flow logs
An IAM permissions boundary

explanation: MFA requires a second authentication factor in addition to the password, so a stolen password alone cannot be used to log in. Config rules and flow logs provide monitoring rather than authentication, and permissions boundaries limit maximum permissions rather than authenticate a user.

stem: A company has 12 AWS accounts and wants employees to sign in once using their existing corporate Active Directory credentials and then access any of the accounts they are authorized for, without creating separate IAM users in each account. Which solution meets this requirement with the least ongoing administrative overhead?

choices.text: Create an IAM user in every account for each employee
Use AWS IAM Identity Center integrated with the corporate directory via AD Connector
Share a single IAM user's access keys across the team
Configure a bastion host that stores credentials for each account

explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center provides centralized single sign-on across multiple AWS accounts and can federate with an on-premises Active Directory via AD Connector, avoiding per-account IAM users. Creating individual IAM users or sharing keys does not scale and violates security best practices.

stem: A security team wants to permanently prevent any IAM principal in a set of member accounts, including account administrators, from disabling AWS CloudTrail, even if their IAM policies would otherwise allow it. Which approach achieves this?

choices.text: Attach an IAM permissions boundary to every user
Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations that denies the CloudTrail stop/delete actions
Add a deny statement to each user's identity-based policy
Enable GuardDuty in the account

explanation: SCPs set the maximum permissions available across all principals in an account, including administrators and root, so a deny SCP blocks the action organization-wide regardless of identity-based policies. Permissions boundaries and per-user policies only affect the principals they are attached to and could be changed by an administrator.

stem: A development team is deploying an application on EC2 instances that needs to call other AWS services such as S3 and DynamoDB. Which approach is the AWS-recommended way to grant this access?

choices.text: Store an IAM user's access key and secret key in the application's configuration file
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance profile
Hardcode the credentials in the application source code
Use the AWS account's root credentials

explanation: Attaching an IAM role to the EC2 instance profile lets the application retrieve automatically rotated, short-lived credentials from instance metadata, eliminating long-term secret management. Storing or hardcoding access keys creates long-lived credentials that are harder to rotate and more exposed.

stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between AWS Regions and Availability Zones (AZs)?

choices.text: Each Availability Zone spans multiple geographic Regions
A Region consists of multiple, isolated Availability Zones connected by low-latency links, each with independent power and networking
An Availability Zone is a single data center shared across all Regions
Regions and Availability Zones are the same construct with different names

explanation: An AWS Region is a geographic area containing two or more Availability Zones, each made up of discrete data centers with independent power, cooling, and networking, connected by high-bandwidth, low-latency links. This lets workloads be architected for fault tolerance by spreading resources across AZs.

stem: A company runs Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) on-premises and wants employees to access the AWS Management Console using their existing corporate credentials, without deploying AWS Directory Service. Which mechanism enables this?

choices.text: IAM users with the same password as AD accounts
SAML 2.0 federation configuring AD FS as an identity provider trusted by IAM, with IAM roles for federated users
A NAT gateway between the corporate network and AWS
AWS Direct Connect alone

explanation: IAM supports SAML 2.0 federation, allowing an on-premises IdP such as AD FS to be registered as a trusted identity provider; authenticated users assume an IAM role to receive temporary credentials for console access. Direct Connect only provides network connectivity and performs no identity federation.

stem: What is the key difference between an identity-based IAM policy and a resource-based policy such as an S3 bucket policy?

choices.text: Identity-based policies are attached to users, groups, or roles, while resource-based policies are attached directly to a resource and can grant access to a principal in another account
Resource-based policies can only deny access, never allow it
Identity-based policies cannot be used with roles
There is no functional difference between the two

explanation: Identity-based policies attach to IAM identities and define what that identity can do, whereas resource-based policies attach to the resource itself and can name a principal, including one from another account, enabling cross-account access. Both policy types can include allow and deny statements.

stem: Team A in Account 111111111111 needs to grant Team B in Account 222222222222 read-only access to objects in an S3 bucket owned by Account A, without creating any IAM users in Account A. Which solution is most appropriate?

choices.text: Enable public read access on the bucket
Attach a bucket policy to the S3 bucket that grants s3:GetObject to Account B's principal ARN
Email the bucket's access keys to Team B
Create a NAT gateway shared between both accounts

explanation: An S3 bucket policy is a resource-based policy that can explicitly grant permissions to a principal in another AWS account, providing controlled cross-account access without exposing the bucket publicly or creating IAM users in the owner account. Public access would expose the data to everyone, not just Team B.

stem: An organization needs a control that sets the maximum permissions for every IAM principal across dozens of member accounts, while a separate team also wants to cap what a specific IAM role can do within one account even if its identity-based policy is broader. Which pairing of controls fits these two requirements respectively?

choices.text: IAM permissions boundary for the organization-wide control; Service Control Policy for the single role
Service Control Policy (SCP) for the organization-wide control; IAM permissions boundary for the single role
Two Service Control Policies, one nested inside the other
Two IAM permissions boundaries applied to the AWS Organizations root

explanation: SCPs are applied at the AWS Organizations level and set maximum permissions for all principals in affected accounts, while an IAM permissions boundary is attached to an individual user or role to cap its permissions within one account. Permissions boundaries cannot be applied organization-wide, and SCPs cannot target a single role.

stem: A company wants to deny all IAM users the ability to delete S3 buckets unless they have authenticated with MFA. Which IAM policy element should be used to enforce this?

choices.text: A resource policy on IAM itself
A Deny statement with a condition using aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to false
An SCP that blocks the S3 service entirely
A permissions boundary with no conditions

explanation: IAM policies support the aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition key; a Deny statement using Bool false on this key blocks the action unless MFA was used on the session. Blocking S3 entirely via SCP would prevent legitimate MFA-authenticated deletions too.

stem: What does AWS Security Token Service (STS) primarily provide?

choices.text: Permanent access keys for IAM users
Temporary, short-lived security credentials for IAM roles or federated users
DNS resolution for VPC resources
Encryption keys for S3 objects

explanation: AWS STS issues temporary security credentials with a limited lifetime for IAM roles, federated users, or cross-account access, reducing the risk associated with long-term credentials. It does not manage encryption keys or DNS.

stem: A company is setting up a multi-account AWS environment from scratch and wants a pre-built landing zone with baseline security guardrails, automated account provisioning, and centralized logging across accounts. Which service should they use?

choices.text: AWS Control Tower
Amazon Inspector
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Config alone

explanation: AWS Control Tower automates the setup of a multi-account landing zone based on best practices, including preventive and detective guardrails built on SCPs and AWS Config, centralized logging, and an account factory. Trusted Advisor and Inspector provide recommendations and vulnerability scanning, not full landing zone orchestration.

stem: What is a key difference between an IAM group and an IAM role?

choices.text: An IAM group can be assumed by an EC2 instance, while a role cannot
An IAM group is a collection of IAM users that share attached policies, while an IAM role is an identity that can be assumed by users, applications, or AWS services to obtain temporary credentials
IAM groups and IAM roles are identical in AWS
IAM roles can only be used by the root user

explanation: IAM groups bundle IAM users so policies can be applied collectively; groups cannot be assumed and have no credentials of their own. IAM roles are assumable identities that provide temporary credentials to users, applications, or services, making them suitable for cross-account access or EC2 permissions.

stem: A developer with an IAM policy that grants s3:PutObject on a bucket reports getting Access Denied errors when uploading, even though no changes were made to their IAM policy. The member account belongs to an AWS Organization. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The S3 bucket does not support PutObject
A Service Control Policy at the OU or account level explicitly denies the s3:PutObject action, which overrides the IAM allow
The developer's password has expired
The bucket is in a different Availability Zone

explanation: In AWS Organizations, an explicit deny in an SCP always overrides an allow in an identity-based or resource-based policy, since effective permissions are the intersection of what the SCP allows and what IAM grants. Password expiration or AZ placement would not produce this specific denial behavior.

stem: Which statement best describes the principle of least privilege in AWS IAM?

choices.text: Granting every principal AdministratorAccess by default and revoking permissions only when abuse is detected
Granting only the minimum set of permissions needed for a principal to perform its intended tasks
Giving all principals read-only access to every service
Disabling IAM entirely and relying on network security only

explanation: Least privilege means granting the minimum permissions necessary for a user, role, or service to accomplish its job, reducing the impact of a compromised credential. Defaulting to administrator access or disabling IAM contradicts this principle and increases risk.

stem: How do security groups differ from network ACLs (NACLs) in a VPC?

choices.text: Security groups are stateless and operate at the subnet level, while NACLs are stateful and operate at the instance level
Security groups are stateful and operate at the instance (ENI) level, while NACLs are stateless and operate at the subnet level
Security groups can only deny traffic, while NACLs can only allow traffic
There is no difference; both are configured identically

explanation: Security groups act as a stateful firewall at the elastic network interface level, automatically allowing return traffic, while NACLs are stateless and applied at the subnet boundary, requiring explicit rules both ways. Both support allow and deny rules, but only NACLs support explicit deny statements.

stem: A company wants its backend database servers to have outbound internet access for software updates but must not be directly reachable from the internet. Which architecture achieves this?

choices.text: Place the database servers in a public subnet with an internet gateway attached
Place the database servers in a private subnet, and route outbound traffic through a NAT gateway in a public subnet
Assign public IP addresses directly to the database servers
Disable all security groups on the database servers

explanation: Placing servers in a private subnet keeps them unreachable directly from the internet, while a NAT gateway in a public subnet allows outbound-only connections such as patch downloads. Public subnets with internet gateways or public IPs would expose the servers directly to the internet.

stem: What is a key difference between AWS Shield Standard and AWS Shield Advanced?

choices.text: Shield Standard is a paid service while Shield Advanced is free

Shield Standard automatically protects all AWS customers at no extra cost against common network/transport layer DDoS attacks, while Shield Advanced is a paid service offering enhanced detection, DDoS cost protection, and 24/7 access to the DDoS Response Team
Shield Advanced only works with Amazon S3
Shield Standard and Shield Advanced provide identical protections

explanation: Shield Standard is automatically enabled for all customers at no extra cost against common DDoS attacks. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription adding advanced detection for larger attacks, cost protection against scaling charges, and DDoS Response Team access.

stem: A security team wants continuous, automated threat detection across their AWS accounts that analyzes VPC flow logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events to identify potentially malicious activity such as compromised instances or unusual API calls. Which service should they enable?

choices.text: AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon Macie

explanation: Amazon GuardDuty continuously analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events using threat intelligence and machine learning to identify malicious or unauthorized activity. AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, and Macie focuses on discovering sensitive data in S3.

stem: Which AWS service uses machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data such as personally identifiable information (PII) stored in Amazon S3?

choices.text: Amazon Macie
AWS Shield
Amazon Inspector
AWS Firewall Manager

explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII stored in S3 buckets, and alerts on data security risks. Inspector focuses on vulnerability scanning of compute resources, not data classification.

stem: A mobile application needs to let end users sign up, sign in, and manage their own profiles, and the development team wants a fully managed service to handle this user directory and authentication flow, including social identity provider login. Which service should they use?

choices.text: AWS IAM Identity Center
Amazon Cognito user pools
AWS Directory Service
AWS Organizations

explanation: Amazon Cognito user pools provide a managed user directory for application sign-up and sign-in, supporting federation with social and SAML/OIDC identity providers, and issuing tokens for application use. IAM Identity Center is designed for workforce access to AWS accounts, not customer-facing app authentication.

stem: An application on an EC2 instance cannot receive inbound HTTPS traffic from clients on the internet, even though the instance has a public IP address and the route table has a route to an internet gateway. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The VPC does not support HTTPS traffic
The security group attached to the instance does not have an inbound rule allowing TCP port 443
The instance is in the wrong Region
NAT gateways always block inbound HTTPS

explanation: Security groups act as a stateful instance-level firewall; without an inbound rule permitting TCP port 443, HTTPS traffic is blocked even with correct routing and public addressing. NAT gateways are unrelated to inbound traffic to a public instance, and Region choice does not affect protocol support.

stem: A financial services company needs a dedicated, private network connection between its data center and AWS with consistent low latency and high bandwidth for a latency-sensitive trading application, and is willing to accept a longer setup lead time to achieve this. Which connectivity option best fits this requirement compared to a Site-to-Site VPN?

choices.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN, because it can be provisioned in minutes
AWS Direct Connect, because it provides a dedicated private network connection with more consistent latency and bandwidth than a VPN over the public internet
Amazon CloudFront, because it caches content closer to users
AWS Transit Gateway alone, without any on-premises connectivity

explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated physical connection between on-premises infrastructure and AWS, bypassing the public internet and providing more predictable latency and higher bandwidth, at the cost of longer provisioning time. VPN is faster to set up but relies on the public internet, introducing variable latency unsuitable for latency-sensitive trading.

stem: What is the primary function of a route table in an Amazon VPC?

choices.text: To encrypt traffic between subnets
To determine where network traffic from a subnet or gateway is directed
To filter traffic based on port number only
To store IAM policies for the VPC

explanation: A route table contains rules that determine where network traffic from a subnet or gateway is directed, such as to an internet gateway, NAT gateway, or peering connection. Traffic filtering by port and protocol is handled by security groups and NACLs, not route tables.

stem: A network engineer adds a NACL rule with rule number 100 to deny all inbound traffic from a specific IP range, but traffic from that range is still reaching instances in the subnet. The NACL already has a rule with number 50 that allows all inbound traffic. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: NACL rules are evaluated in order from the lowest rule number, so rule 50 (allow all) is matched first and rule 100 is never evaluated
Security groups always override NACLs
NACLs do not support deny rules
NACL rules are evaluated in reverse alphabetical order

explanation: NACL rules are evaluated in ascending order of rule number, and the first matching rule applies; since rule 50 allows all inbound traffic and has a lower number, it is matched first and the deny rule is never reached. NACLs fully support explicit deny rules, and security groups do not override NACL evaluation order.

stem: A company runs a public-facing web application and wants to build a layered defense against both large-scale volumetric DDoS attacks and application-layer attacks like HTTP floods and malicious request patterns. Which combination of services provides this defense in depth?

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront and AWS Shield Advanced for edge-level DDoS absorption, combined with AWS WAF for application-layer filtering
Security groups alone
Amazon Macie and AWS Config
AWS Direct Connect and AWS Trusted Advisor

explanation: CloudFront combined with Shield Advanced absorbs and mitigates large volumetric and protocol DDoS attacks at the edge, while WAF inspects application-layer HTTP requests to block malicious patterns such as floods or injection attempts. Security groups alone cannot inspect HTTP content or absorb large-scale volumetric attacks.

stem: A company is deciding between using a NAT gateway and a self-managed NAT instance to provide outbound internet access for private subnet resources. Which statement accurately compares the two?

choices.text: A NAT instance is a managed AWS service requiring no maintenance, while a NAT gateway must be patched manually
A NAT gateway is a fully managed, highly available AWS service, while a NAT instance is a customer-managed EC2 instance requiring patching and manual scaling
NAT gateways cannot scale bandwidth, unlike NAT instances
NAT instances and NAT gateways provide identical management overhead

explanation: An AWS-managed NAT gateway automatically scales bandwidth and is highly available within an AZ without customer patching, whereas a NAT instance is a regular EC2 instance the customer must patch and manage for scaling and availability. This makes NAT gateways preferable for most production workloads.

stem: What is the primary security benefit of segmenting a VPC into public and private subnets?

choices.text: It reduces the AWS bill automatically
It limits direct internet exposure of backend resources by placing them in subnets without a route to an internet gateway, while internet-facing resources reside in public subnets
It increases the number of Availability Zones automatically
It removes the need for security groups

explanation: Segmentation limits the attack surface by ensuring only resources that must be internet-facing reside in public subnets with a route to an internet gateway, while backend resources like databases remain in private subnets, unreachable directly from the internet. It does not affect billing, AZ count, or eliminate the need for security groups.

stem: A security team wants to block common SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) patterns in incoming web requests without writing custom detection logic from scratch. What is the most efficient way to achieve this with AWS WAF?

choices.text: Write a fully custom Lambda function for every possible attack signature
Use AWS Managed Rules for WAF, such as the SQL database and Core Rule Set (CRS) managed rule groups
Disable WAF and rely solely on security groups
Configure a NACL to inspect HTTP payloads

explanation: AWS Managed Rules for WAF include preconfigured rule groups, such as the SQL database rule group and Core Rule Set, maintained by AWS that protect against common exploits like SQL injection and XSS without custom rule authoring. NACLs operate at Layer 3/4 and cannot inspect HTTP payload content.

stem: An application architecture has a web tier and a database tier, both running on Auto Scaling groups whose instances change frequently. Which security group configuration best accommodates this dynamic scaling while maintaining least privilege?

choices.text: Reference the web tier's security group as the source in the database tier's inbound rule, instead of hardcoding IP address ranges
Allow inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on the database tier
Manually update the database security group's IP allow list every time an instance launches or terminates
Disable security groups on the database tier and rely only on NACLs

explanation: Referencing a security group as the source of a rule automatically includes any instance associated with that group, so the rule stays accurate as instances scale without manual updates, unlike static CIDR-based rules. Allowing 0.0.0.0/0 or disabling security groups would violate least privilege and expose the database tier broadly.

stem: A company needs to establish secure connectivity between its on-premises network and a VPC within a few hours, with encryption in transit, and can tolerate variable latency since the workload is not latency-sensitive. Which option best meets this need?

choices.text: AWS Direct Connect, because it can be provisioned within hours
AWS Site-to-Site VPN, because it can typically be configured quickly and encrypts traffic over an IPsec tunnel across the internet
Amazon CloudFront
A VPC peering connection to an unrelated VPC

explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec tunnels over the public internet and can typically be set up quickly, making it suitable when rapid, encrypted connectivity is needed and some latency variability is acceptable. Direct Connect provides more consistent performance but generally takes weeks to months to provision due to physical circuit installation.

stem: When an S3 object is encrypted using SSE-KMS, which statement best describes how the encryption process works?

choices.text: S3 encrypts the object directly with the KMS master key on every request
S3 uses envelope encryption: KMS generates a unique data key to encrypt the object, and the data key itself is encrypted by the KMS customer master key (CMK)
The object is encrypted using a password chosen by the uploading user
Encryption only occurs when the object is downloaded, not when uploaded

explanation: SSE-KMS uses envelope encryption, where KMS generates a unique data encryption key per object that encrypts the object, and the data key itself is encrypted under the KMS key and stored with the object. This avoids using the KMS key directly on bulk data, improving performance and key protection.

stem: Which AWS service allows you to provision, manage, and deploy public and private TLS/SSL certificates for use with services like Elastic Load Balancing and CloudFront to encrypt data in transit?

choices.text: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
AWS Key Management Service (KMS)
AWS Secrets Manager
Amazon Macie

explanation: AWS Certificate Manager provisions and manages public and private SSL/TLS certificates, integrating with services such as Elastic Load Balancing and CloudFront to enable HTTPS and encrypt data in transit. KMS manages encryption keys for data at rest and cryptographic operations, not TLS certificate issuance.

stem: A company uses AWS Certificate Manager to issue a public certificate for its Application Load Balancer and wants to avoid manual certificate renewal and the risk of an expired certificate causing an outage. What should they do?

choices.text: Manually track the expiration date and re-issue the certificate each year
Use an ACM-issued certificate, which is automatically renewed by ACM as long as domain validation can be completed
Export the certificate and store it on each server
Switch to a self-signed certificate to avoid renewal

explanation: Public certificates issued by ACM are automatically renewed before expiration provided domain validation can still be completed, such as DNS validation records remaining in place, removing manual renewal effort. Manually tracking expiration or using self-signed certificates increases operational risk and forgoes ACM's automation.

stem: A user has an IAM policy that grants kms:Decrypt on a specific KMS key, but the user still receives an Access Denied error when attempting to decrypt data with that key. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: IAM policies never apply to KMS

The KMS key's key policy does not grant the calling principal or account permission to use the key, and since KMS key policies act as the resource policy, both the key policy and IAM policy must allow the action
The key is in a different Region
KMS keys cannot be used for decryption

explanation: For a caller to use a KMS key, both the key policy and the caller's IAM policy must allow the action; unless the key policy grants the account or specific principal permission, an IAM allow alone is insufficient. Region mismatch or an inability to decrypt do not apply since a valid key was targeted.

stem: A company wants to protect critical S3 data against accidental deletion and also maintain a copy in a second AWS Region for disaster recovery. Which combination of features should be enabled?

choices.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering only
S3 Versioning combined with Cross-Region Replication (CRR)
S3 Transfer Acceleration
Disabling bucket policies

explanation: S3 Versioning preserves previous object versions, protecting against accidental overwrites or deletions, and Cross-Region Replication automatically copies objects to a bucket in another Region for disaster recovery. Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage cost and provides neither versioning nor cross-region redundancy.

stem: What is the primary purpose of data classification in a data governance strategy?

choices.text: To automatically encrypt all data regardless of sensitivity
To categorize data based on sensitivity and criticality so that appropriate handling, access, and protection controls can be applied
To determine which AWS Region has the lowest cost
To replace the need for encryption entirely

explanation: Data classification categorizes data, for example public, internal, confidential, or restricted, based on sensitivity and business impact, which informs the appropriate access controls, encryption requirements, and retention policies. It does not itself perform encryption or relate to Region cost selection.

stem: A company runs workloads using EBS volumes, RDS databases, and DynamoDB tables and wants to centrally define and enforce backup schedules, retention periods, and cross-region copy policies across all of these resource types from a single service. Which service should they use?

choices.text: AWS Backup
Amazon S3 Glacier
AWS Config
AWS Trusted Advisor

explanation: AWS Backup is a fully managed service that centralizes and automates backup policies across multiple AWS services, including EBS, RDS, and DynamoDB, supporting scheduled backups, retention rules, and cross-region or cross-account copying from a single console. AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance rather than performing backups.

stem: Account A wants to allow a role in Account B to decrypt objects encrypted with a customer managed KMS key owned by Account A. The role in Account B has an IAM policy allowing kms:Decrypt, but decryption still fails. What additional configuration is most likely missing?

choices.text: The KMS key's key policy must explicitly allow the external account or role as a principal to use the key
KMS keys can never be shared across accounts
The S3 bucket policy needs to allow kms:Decrypt instead
Account B needs a Direct Connect connection to Account A

explanation: Cross-account use of a customer managed KMS key requires the key policy in the owning account to grant permission to the external account or principal, in addition to an IAM policy in the calling account; without this key policy grant, the request is denied regardless of the IAM policy. KMS keys can be shared cross-account via key policies, and Direct Connect is unrelated to KMS authorization.

stem: A financial company must retain certain records in Amazon S3 in a way that prevents them from being deleted or overwritten by any user, including the root account, for a fixed retention period, to meet regulatory requirements. Which S3 feature should be used?

choices.text: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access storage class
S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 bucket policies alone

explanation: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode implements a WORM model that prevents an object version from being deleted or overwritten by any user, including the root account, until the retention period expires, satisfying regulatory retention requirements. Storage class selection and bucket policies alone do not provide this immutability guarantee.

stem: A company wants to encrypt all new EBS volumes in an account by default using a customer managed KMS key rather than the AWS managed default key, without requiring developers to manually specify encryption settings each time. What should they configure?

choices.text: Enable EBS encryption by default at the account/Region level and set the customer managed key as the default encryption key
Manually re-encrypt each volume after creation
Disable KMS entirely and rely on S3 encryption
Attach an IAM policy that mentions encryption in its name

explanation: EC2 supports enabling encryption by default for EBS volumes per account/Region, and administrators can specify a customer managed KMS key as the default, so all newly created volumes and snapshots are automatically encrypted without developer action. Manually re-encrypting afterward is burdensome and does not prevent unencrypted volumes from being created initially.

stem: A company needs full control over a KMS key's access policy, the ability to enable or disable the key, and the ability to define custom key rotation and deletion schedules, in order to meet a strict compliance requirement. Which type of KMS key should they use?

choices.text: An AWS owned key
An AWS managed key
A customer managed key
There is no difference between the three key types for this purpose

explanation: Customer managed keys give the account full control, including editing the key policy, enabling/disabling the key, configuring rotation, and scheduling deletion, satisfying strict compliance requirements. AWS managed keys have a fixed rotation and an unmodifiable key policy, and AWS owned keys are not visible or manageable within the customer's account.

stem: Which AWS service or resource provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports, such as SOC and PCI DSS reports, to help customers demonstrate their own compliance posture?

choices.text: AWS Artifact
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector

explanation: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal providing on-demand access to AWS's compliance reports and select agreements, such as SOC reports and PCI DSS attestations, supporting customer audits. Trusted Advisor gives optimization recommendations and Config tracks resource configuration, neither providing compliance certification documents.

stem: A company generates large volumes of log data in S3 that are frequently accessed for 30 days, rarely accessed for the next 60 days, and then must be retained for 7 years for compliance at the lowest possible cost, with retrieval times of several hours being acceptable. Which S3 feature should be used to automate this data lifecycle?

choices.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Lifecycle policies transitioning objects to S3 Standard-IA, then to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Cross-Region Replication only
S3 Requester Pays

explanation: S3 Lifecycle policies can automatically transition objects between storage classes based on age, moving infrequently accessed data to Standard-IA and then to a low-cost archival tier like Glacier Deep Archive for long-term compliance retention, matching the described pattern and cost goals. Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads and Cross-Region Replication addresses redundancy, neither managing storage-class transitions over time.

stem: A company configured S3 Cross-Region Replication for a bucket encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, but replicated objects in the destination Region fail to decrypt properly for applications there. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The source bucket's KMS key is a single-Region key, and CRR requires either the correct destination-Region KMS key configured in the replication rule or a multi-Region key
Cross-Region Replication does not support encrypted objects at all
The destination bucket must be unencrypted
IAM roles cannot be used with S3 replication

explanation: When replicating KMS-encrypted objects across Regions, the replication configuration must specify a KMS key valid in the destination Region, since a single-Region source key cannot be used there; AWS KMS multi-Region keys or an appropriate destination-Region key resolve this. S3 replication does support encrypted objects when configured correctly, and it does require an IAM role to perform replication.

stem: A company in a highly regulated industry must use a dedicated, single-tenant hardware security module where they retain sole administrative control over the HSM, rather than a shared multi-tenant key management service. Which AWS service meets this requirement?

choices.text: AWS KMS with AWS managed keys
AWS CloudHSM
Amazon Macie
AWS Certificate Manager

explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-2 validated hardware security modules within the customer's VPC, giving exclusive administrative control over the HSM and key material, suiting strict regulatory requirements. AWS KMS, while highly secure, operates as a shared multi-tenant managed service where AWS manages the underlying hardware.

stem: What is the fundamental difference between encryption at rest and encryption in transit?

choices.text: Encryption at rest protects data while it is stored (such as on disk), while encryption in transit protects data as it moves across a network
Encryption at rest only applies to Amazon S3
Encryption in transit is only relevant for on-premises networks
They are two names for the same concept

explanation: Encryption at rest protects stored data, for example on EBS volumes, S3 objects, or database storage, typically using KMS, while encryption in transit, such as TLS/SSL often via ACM certificates, protects data as it is transmitted over a network. These are distinct protections addressing different points in the data lifecycle and are often used together.

stem: A company's disaster recovery plan requires a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of near-zero data loss and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of a few minutes for a critical relational database, in the event an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. Which approach best supports these objectives?

choices.text: Nightly manual database snapshots copied to another Region
Amazon RDS with a cross-Region read replica (or Aurora Global Database) that can be promoted to a standalone primary in the secondary Region
Weekly exports to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Relying solely on Multi-AZ within a single Region

explanation: A cross-Region read replica, or Aurora Global Database with sub-minute cross-region replication lag and fast promotion, minimizes data loss and allows rapid failover if an entire Region becomes unavailable. Nightly snapshots or weekly exports would cause far greater data loss and longer recovery, and Multi-AZ alone only protects against an AZ failure within the same Region, not a full Region outage.

stem: A serverless application receives bursty traffic that occasionally exceeds the backend Lambda function's concurrency, causing downstream throttling. The architect wants API Gateway to smooth incoming traffic spikes before they reach Lambda, without changing client behavior. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Configure a usage plan with rate and burst throttle limits on the API Gateway stage or method
Set the Lambda function's reserved concurrency to unlimited
Enable API Gateway response caching for all methods
Move the API behind an S3 static website

explanation: Throttle settings in an API Gateway usage plan cap the rate and burst of requests reaching the backend, protecting Lambda from overload. Caching only helps repeated read responses, not write bursts; there is no such thing as unlimited reserved concurrency; an S3 static site is unrelated to API traffic shaping.

stem: A financial partner requires SFTP access to exchange files, but the company wants uploaded files to land directly in Amazon S3 without operating any SFTP servers themselves. Which service meets this requirement?

choices.text: AWS Transfer Family
AWS DataSync
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
AWS Storage Gateway

explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides fully managed SFTP, FTPS, and FTP endpoints that can store transferred files directly in S3 (or EFS) without managing server infrastructure. DataSync moves data between existing storage systems rather than exposing an SFTP endpoint, and FSx/Storage Gateway do not provide managed SFTP-to-S3 ingestion.

stem: A read-heavy web application repeatedly queries an RDS MySQL database for product catalog data that rarely changes. The architect wants an in-memory cache in front of the database to reduce latency and load. Which service is the best fit?

choices.text: Amazon ElastiCache
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS Global Accelerator
Amazon CloudFront

explanation: ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) is purpose-built for in-memory caching of database query results, cutting latency and database load. CloudFront caches HTTP content at edge locations rather than arbitrary database query results, Global Accelerator optimizes network paths, and Transfer Acceleration only speeds up S3 uploads.

stem: An architect is choosing between a write-through and a lazy-loading (cache-aside) strategy for an ElastiCache layer in front of a database. Which statement correctly describes a tradeoff of the write-through strategy?

choices.text: Write-through keeps the cache consistently up to date on every write, but adds write latency and can fill the cache with data that is never read
Lazy loading always guarantees the cache never contains stale data
Write-through eliminates the need to ever set a TTL on cached items
Lazy loading writes every database update directly into the cache before the write completes

explanation: Write-through updates the cache synchronously with every database write, keeping data fresh at the cost of added write latency and potentially caching rarely-read data. Lazy loading can serve stale data until expiry (making B false), a TTL is still recommended even with write-through (making C false), and lazy loading only populates the cache after a read miss, not on writes (making D false).

stem: Which statement best differentiates Amazon SNS from Amazon SQS in an event-driven architecture?

choices.text: SNS is a pub/sub service that pushes messages to multiple subscribers, while SQS is a queue that holds messages until a consumer polls and processes them
SNS guarantees exactly-once processing while SQS provides no ordering options at all
SQS pushes messages to subscribers while SNS requires consumers to poll
SNS and SQS provide identical delivery models and are fully interchangeable

explanation: SNS is a push-based publish/subscribe service that fans out to many endpoint types, while SQS is a pull-based queue used to decouple a producer from one or more consumers that poll for messages. Option C reverses the push/pull model, and B and D mischaracterize their delivery and ordering guarantees.

stem: An application running on a single EC2 instance is hitting CPU limits during peak hours. The architect resizes the instance to a type with more vCPUs and memory. This is an example of which scaling approach?

choices.text: Vertical scaling
Horizontal scaling
Auto Scaling
Cross-Region scaling

explanation: Increasing the capacity of a single existing instance is vertical scaling (scaling up), whereas horizontal scaling would add more instances of the same size. Auto Scaling automates horizontal scaling, and cross-Region scaling refers to distributing workloads geographically, not resizing a single instance.

stem: A stateless web tier must handle unpredictable traffic spikes with minimal risk of downtime if any single component fails. Compared to repeatedly resizing one instance, which scaling strategy is generally preferred for this goal?

choices.text: Horizontal scaling using an Auto Scaling group distributed across multiple instances and Availability Zones
Vertical scaling by continually upgrading to larger instance types
Consolidating the workload onto a single larger on-premises server
Disabling health checks so instances are never replaced

explanation: Horizontal scaling spreads load across many instances, so the failure of any single instance does not take down the whole tier, and it has effectively no upper capacity limit. Vertical scaling still leaves a single point of failure and a hardware ceiling, and disabling health checks reduces resilience rather than improving it.

stem: A media company wants to cache video content close to end users worldwide to reduce latency and offload their origin server. Which service should they use?

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront
AWS Direct Connect
Amazon Route 53
AWS Transit Gateway

explanation: CloudFront is AWS's content delivery network, caching content at globally distributed edge locations to reduce latency and offload the origin. Direct Connect is a dedicated network link, Route 53 is a DNS service, and Transit Gateway connects VPCs and networks; none of them cache content.

stem: An application requires content-based routing so that requests to /api/* go to one target group and requests to /images/* go to another, all behind a single load balancer. Which load balancer type supports this natively?

choices.text: Application Load Balancer
Network Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer

explanation: An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and supports path-based and host-based routing rules to different target groups. Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 without content-based routing, Classic Load Balancer lacks advanced routing rules, and Gateway Load Balancer is designed for deploying third-party virtual appliances.

stem: In a typical three-tier web architecture on AWS, which combination correctly maps services to the presentation, application, and data tiers respectively?

choices.text: CloudFront/ALB for presentation, an EC2 or ECS Auto Scaling group for application logic, and RDS/Aurora for data
S3 for presentation, Route 53 for application logic, and IAM for data
Lambda for presentation, CloudTrail for application logic, and CloudWatch for data
WAF for presentation, KMS for application logic, and Secrets Manager for data

explanation: A classic three-tier design fronts requests with CloudFront/ALB, runs business logic on scalable compute such as EC2, ECS, or Lambda, and persists data in a database tier like RDS or Aurora. The other options assign services (DNS, IAM, logging, security tooling) to tiers whose actual function they do not serve.

stem: A team needs to run a long-running batch container process, lasting several hours and requiring more memory than AWS Lambda's maximum, without managing any servers. Which service is more appropriate than Lambda?

choices.text: AWS Fargate
An EC2 Spot Fleet managed entirely by custom scaling scripts
AWS Lambda with its timeout extended beyond 15 minutes
Amazon S3 Batch Operations

explanation: Fargate runs containers with higher memory and CPU ceilings and no fixed execution time limit, while remaining serverless from an infrastructure-management perspective. Lambda cannot exceed its 15-minute maximum timeout, and S3 Batch Operations only performs bulk operations on S3 objects, not general-purpose long-running compute.

stem: A Lambda function that processes S3 upload events intermittently times out under heavy concurrent load, and CloudWatch metrics show a high number of throttled invocations. What is the most likely cause and remedy?

choices.text: The function or account concurrency limit is being reached; request a service quota increase or configure reserved/provisioned concurrency appropriately
The S3 bucket lacks sufficient durability; enable versioning to fix the throttling
The Lambda function needs a larger attached EBS volume
The event source is being throttled by an expired IAM access key

explanation: Sustained throttling under high concurrency typically indicates the account or per-function concurrency limit has been reached; requesting a quota increase or tuning reserved/provisioned concurrency addresses this directly. Lambda does not use attached EBS volumes, S3 versioning is unrelated to throttling, and Lambda invocations are not throttled via IAM access keys.

stem: A company needs a shared, POSIX-compliant file system that can be concurrently mounted by hundreds of Linux EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Which storage option is appropriate?

choices.text: Amazon EFS
Amazon EBS
Amazon S3
EC2 instance store

explanation: EFS is a fully managed, POSIX-compliant elastic file system supporting concurrent access from many instances across multiple AZs. Standard EBS volumes attach to a single instance at a time, S3 is object storage rather than a POSIX file system, and instance store is ephemeral, local storage tied to one instance.

stem: A database workload requires low-latency, high-IOPS block storage attached to a single EC2 instance. Which storage option correctly satisfies this need?

choices.text: Amazon EBS, using a provisioned-IOPS volume type such as io2
Amazon S3 Standard
Amazon EFS
Amazon S3 Glacier

explanation: EBS provides block storage with provisioned IOPS volume types (such as io1/io2) suited for low-latency, high-throughput database workloads. S3 and Glacier are object storage optimized for durability and cost rather than low-latency block access, and EFS is a shared file system rather than block storage for a single instance.

stem: In Amazon ECS, which component is responsible for maintaining the desired number of running copies of a task definition and replacing any tasks that fail?

choices.text: An ECS Service
An ECS Task Definition
An ECS Cluster
The ECS Container Agent

explanation: An ECS Service maintains a specified desired count of running tasks derived from a task definition and automatically replaces unhealthy or stopped tasks. The Task Definition only describes container configuration, the Cluster is the logical grouping of compute resources, and the Container Agent runs on EC2 instances to communicate with the ECS control plane.

stem: A read-heavy reporting workload is degrading performance on the primary RDS MySQL instance that also handles transactional writes. What is the most effective way to offload the read traffic without impacting write performance?

choices.text: Create one or more RDS read replicas and direct reporting queries to them
Increase the primary instance's allocated storage size
Enable a Multi-AZ standby for the primary instance
Move the workload to a single, larger instance class only

explanation: Read replicas asynchronously replicate from the primary and can serve read-only queries, offloading reporting traffic from the primary instance. A Multi-AZ standby exists for failover/availability rather than serving read traffic in typical configurations, and simply increasing storage or instance size does not specifically separate read from write load.

stem: A photo-sharing application processes uploaded images through resizing, watermarking, and thumbnail-generation steps. The architect wants each step to scale independently and remain resilient to failures in the other steps. Which approach best achieves this loose coupling?

choices.text: Chain the steps using separate SQS queues (or an event bus) between independent worker services, each polling or reacting to its own queue or event
Combine all processing into a single monolithic Lambda function invoked synchronously by the upload handler
Run all processing steps within one EC2 instance to simplify communication
Use direct in-process function calls between the resizing, watermarking, and thumbnail components

explanation: Using queues or events between independent workers lets each processing step scale and fail independently of the others, which is the essence of loose coupling. A monolithic function, a single instance, or direct in-process calls all create tight coupling where a bottleneck or failure in one step affects the entire pipeline.

stem: Which AWS construct represents one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity, located within an AWS Region?

choices.text: Availability Zone
Edge location
Local Zone
Region

explanation: An Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers with redundant infrastructure, isolated from failures in other AZs within the same Region. A Region is the broader geographic area containing multiple AZs, edge locations are CloudFront caching points, and Local Zones extend AWS infrastructure closer to specific metro areas.

stem: A company wants DNS-based failover so that if the primary application endpoint in one Region becomes unhealthy, traffic automatically routes to a standby endpoint in another Region. Which Route 53 routing policy should be used?

choices.text: Failover routing policy
Simple routing policy
Geolocation routing policy
Multivalue answer routing policy

explanation: Route 53 failover routing works with health checks to route to a primary resource and automatically switch to a secondary resource when the primary fails a health check. Simple routing has no health-check-driven failover, geolocation routes based on user location rather than health, and multivalue answer returns several healthy records but is not intended as a primary/standby failover mechanism.

stem: An architecture needs to convert customer support text tickets into spoken audio for an accessibility feature, without managing any machine learning infrastructure. Which AWS managed service should be used?

choices.text: Amazon Polly
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Rekognition

explanation: Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike spoken audio (text-to-speech). Comprehend performs natural language processing such as sentiment analysis rather than speech synthesis, Transcribe converts speech into text (the opposite direction), and Rekognition analyzes images and video.

stem: EC2 instances in a private subnet cannot reach the internet through a NAT gateway, even though the NAT gateway is running and has an Elastic IP address. What is the most likely misconfiguration to check first?

choices.text: The private subnet's route table lacks a route (such as 0.0.0.0/0) pointing to the NAT gateway
A security group attached directly to the NAT gateway is blocking outbound traffic
An internet gateway is attached to the private subnet instead of the public subnet
The private instances are missing their own Elastic IP addresses

explanation: For private subnet instances to reach the internet through a NAT gateway, the private subnet's route table must contain a default route to that NAT gateway. NAT gateways do not use security groups, internet gateways attach at the VPC level rather than to a specific subnet, and private instances should not be assigned public or Elastic IP addresses.

stem: A VPC has a public subnet that must reach the internet directly and a private subnet that must reach the internet only through a NAT gateway. Which statement correctly describes the required route table configuration?

choices.text: The public subnet's route table has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway, and the private subnet's route table has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to a NAT gateway that resides in the public subnet
Both subnets should have a 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing directly to the internet gateway
Only the VPC's main route table needs to be configured; individual subnet route tables are unnecessary
The private subnet should route to the internet gateway, and the public subnet should route through the NAT gateway

explanation: Standard VPC design routes public subnet traffic directly to an internet gateway, while private subnet traffic routes to a NAT gateway (itself placed in a public subnet, using the internet gateway on the private instances' behalf). Options B and D swap the gateways incorrectly, and distinct subnet route tables are required to achieve this differentiated routing, making C incorrect.

stem: Which disaster recovery strategy involves keeping only the minimal, always-on core of an application (such as a small replicated database) running in a secondary Region, which can be rapidly scaled up when a disaster occurs?

choices.text: Pilot light
Backup and restore
Multi-site active-active
Warm standby

explanation: Pilot light keeps only critical core components running at minimal capacity in the DR Region, ready to be scaled up quickly, much like a pilot light that can ignite a full flame. Backup and restore has no running infrastructure until recovery time, warm standby runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the whole system, and active-active runs full capacity simultaneously in both sites.

stem: A company wants the lowest possible RTO and RPO and is willing to pay to run full production capacity simultaneously in two Regions, actively serving live traffic from both. Which DR strategy does this describe?

choices.text: Multi-site active-active
Pilot light
Backup and restore
Warm standby

explanation: Multi-site active-active runs full workloads simultaneously in multiple Regions, providing near-zero RTO and RPO but at the highest cost of the common DR strategies. Pilot light and warm standby run reduced-capacity secondary environments, and backup and restore has the highest RTO and RPO among the four.

stem: A company's disaster recovery plan states that after an incident, it can tolerate losing up to 1 hour of data and must restore service within 4 hours. Which pair of terms correctly describes these two targets, respectively?

choices.text: RPO of 1 hour, RTO of 4 hours
RTO of 1 hour, RPO of 4 hours
MTTR of 1 hour, MTBF of 4 hours
SLA of 1 hour, SLO of 4 hours

explanation: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) measures the maximum acceptable data loss, here 1 hour, while Recovery Time Objective (RTO) measures the maximum acceptable downtime, here 4 hours. MTTR/MTBF describe repair and failure-interval statistics, and SLA/SLO describe service-level commitments, neither of which is the standard terminology for DR data-loss and downtime targets.

stem: A company is choosing between a warm standby and a pilot light disaster recovery strategy for a critical application. Which statement correctly describes a key tradeoff between the two?

choices.text: Warm standby runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the application continuously, enabling faster recovery than pilot light, but at higher ongoing cost
Pilot light and warm standby have identical RTO and cost profiles
Warm standby never keeps any compute running until failover, making it cheaper than pilot light
Pilot light requires full-scale production capacity running at all times in the DR Region

explanation: Warm standby keeps a reduced but functioning full application stack running continuously, so failover mainly requires scaling up, achieving a faster RTO than pilot light (which only keeps core components running) but at greater ongoing cost. Options C and D reverse the actual definitions of the two strategies.

stem: In a distributed architecture, which pattern involves retrying a failed operation with progressively longer delays between attempts, often with randomization, to avoid overwhelming a recovering service?

choices.text: Exponential backoff with jitter
Circuit breaker
Bulkhead
Fan-out

explanation: Exponential backoff increases the delay between successive retries, and adding jitter randomizes that delay to avoid synchronized retry storms against a recovering service. A circuit breaker stops calls entirely rather than retrying with delay, a bulkhead isolates resources to contain failures, and fan-out distributes a single event to multiple consumers.

stem: An RDS Multi-AZ deployment experiences an unplanned outage on its primary instance. What happens automatically to maintain availability?

choices.text: RDS automatically fails over to the synchronously replicated standby in another Availability Zone and repoints the existing DNS endpoint to it
The application must be manually reconfigured with a new database endpoint
RDS creates a brand-new read replica in the same Availability Zone to replace the primary
Data is unavailable until an administrator manually restores from the latest snapshot

explanation: RDS Multi-AZ automatically detects failure of the primary instance and fails over to its synchronously replicated standby, typically within about one to two minutes, while the existing DNS endpoint is updated to point at the new primary. No manual endpoint change, new replica creation, or snapshot restore is required for this automatic failover.

stem: An application uses Route 53 health checks with failover routing to a secondary Region, but during a recent primary Region outage, failover did not occur even though the primary was clearly unavailable. What is a likely cause?

choices.text: The Route 53 health check was not configured to monitor the actual endpoint or path that was actually failing
The secondary Region's resources were deployed in a different VPC than the primary
The primary Region had more Availability Zones configured than the secondary Region
The DNS record's TTL was set too low, preventing resolvers from caching it

explanation: Route 53 failover depends entirely on the health check accurately reflecting the resource's true health; if it targets the wrong endpoint or path, or has misconfigured thresholds, it can report the resource as healthy when it is not, preventing failover. Differing VPCs or AZ counts between Regions, and a low TTL (which actually speeds up failover propagation), are not the underlying cause of a failed health-check-driven failover.

stem: Which deployment practice involves never modifying running servers in place; instead, any change requires deploying entirely new instances built from a fresh, versioned machine image?

choices.text: Immutable infrastructure
Blue/green in-place patching
Rolling in-place configuration management
Manual SSH-based hotfixing

explanation: Immutable infrastructure replaces servers with new instances built from a new image instead of altering existing ones, reducing configuration drift and improving consistency and reliability. In-place patching, rolling configuration management, and manual hotfixing all modify running servers, which is the opposite of the immutable approach.

stem: To ensure high availability, an Application Load Balancer's targets should be configured across which of the following?

choices.text: Registered targets spread across multiple Availability Zones
A single Availability Zone only, to minimize latency
A single EC2 instance, for simplicity
On-premises servers exclusively, since ALB cannot target AWS resources

explanation: For high availability, an ALB's targets should span multiple Availability Zones so the failure of one AZ does not take down the entire application, and the ALB itself is inherently distributed across AZs. Restricting targets to a single AZ or a single instance removes redundancy, and ALB can target AWS resources such as EC2, ECS, and Lambda in addition to on-premises IP targets.

stem: Some targets behind an Application Load Balancer are being marked unhealthy and removed from rotation, reducing overall capacity during peak load, even though the application appears to be running normally. What should the architect check first?

choices.text: The target group's health check configuration, such as the path, interval, and healthy/unhealthy thresholds, to confirm it matches what the application actually returns
The Route 53 TTL settings configured for the application's domain
The AWS account's service quota for the number of VPCs
The CloudFront cache behavior settings for the distribution

explanation: ALB target health is determined entirely by its configured health check; a mismatched path or overly strict thresholds can cause otherwise healthy targets to be marked unhealthy and removed from rotation. Route 53 TTL, VPC quotas, and CloudFront cache behaviors have no bearing on ALB target health check evaluation.

stem: What is a key resilience benefit of using Amazon RDS Proxy during a database failover event?

choices.text: RDS Proxy maintains established connections and quickly redirects them to the new primary, reducing the failover time perceived by the application
RDS Proxy prevents any database failover from ever occurring
RDS Proxy eliminates the need to configure Multi-AZ deployments
RDS Proxy automatically encrypts all data at rest
RDS Proxy removes the need for a database endpoint entirely

explanation: RDS Proxy pools connections and can significantly reduce the failover time an application experiences by quickly redirecting to the new primary after a failover. It does not prevent failovers from occurring, does not replace Multi-AZ (the two features complement each other), and has no role in encryption at rest.

stem: What is the best practice when an application is expected to approach or exceed a default AWS service quota, such as the EC2 On-Demand vCPU limit, due to planned growth?

choices.text: Proactively request a service quota increase through the Service Quotas console or AWS Support before the limit is reached
Take no action, since AWS automatically raises all quotas without any request
Switch entirely to a different AWS Region to permanently bypass the quota
Delete unused IAM roles to increase the available quota

explanation: AWS service quotas can typically be increased by requesting a change through the Service Quotas console or AWS Support, and doing so proactively before hitting the limit avoids service disruption. Quotas are not automatically raised without a request in general, quotas are generally tracked per Region so switching Regions does not eliminate the constraint, and IAM roles are unrelated to compute quotas.

stem: Amazon S3 Standard is designed to provide how many nines of durability for stored objects, achieved by automatically redundantly storing data across multiple Availability Zones?

choices.text: 99.999999999 percent (11 nines)
99.9 percent (three nines)
99.99 percent (four nines)
99.95 percent, which is actually an availability figure rather than a durability figure

explanation: S3 Standard is designed for 99.999999999 percent (eleven nines) of object durability by redundantly storing data across multiple Availability Zones within a Region. The other percentages listed correspond to typical availability SLA figures for various services, not S3's durability design target.

stem: A company must retain a copy of critical S3 objects in a separate AWS Region to protect against a full Regional disaster, with new objects automatically copied as they are created. Which S3 feature should be enabled?

choices.text: S3 Cross-Region Replication
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Object Lock

explanation: Cross-Region Replication automatically and asynchronously copies new objects to a bucket in a different Region, protecting against a Regional-scale failure. Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage cost across access tiers, Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads over long distances, and Object Lock provides write-once-read-many protection, none of which replicate objects across Regions.

stem: A distributed application spans API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB, and the team needs to trace individual requests end-to-end to identify which component is causing intermittent latency. Which service should they use?

choices.text: AWS X-Ray
Amazon CloudWatch Logs alone
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector

explanation: AWS X-Ray provides distributed tracing across services, generating a service map and per-segment latency data that pinpoints bottlenecks along a request's full path. CloudWatch Logs alone shows per-service logs without correlated tracing across the call chain, AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, and Amazon Inspector performs security assessments; none of these trace individual requests end-to-end.

stem: A three-tier application currently runs its web tier across multiple Availability Zones behind an ALB, but the entire database tier is a single RDS instance in one Availability Zone with no standby. Which single change would most directly eliminate the database as a single point of failure?

choices.text: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS instance
Add more read replicas within the same Availability Zone as the primary
Increase the RDS instance's allocated storage size
Move the database to a larger instance class within the same Availability Zone

explanation: Multi-AZ deployment provisions a synchronously replicated standby in a different Availability Zone with automatic failover, directly removing the dependency on a single AZ as a point of failure. Adding read replicas in the same AZ, increasing storage, or upsizing the instance class do not address the underlying single-AZ point of failure.

stem: A financial services company runs a self-managed relational database on an EC2 instance that requires sustained 64,000 IOPS with sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability. Which EBS volume type should the solutions architect choose to meet this requirement?

choices.text: gp3
st1
io2 Block Express
sc1

explanation: io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS and sub-millisecond latency with 99.999% durability, designed for the most demanding, IO-intensive workloads. gp3 tops out at 16,000 IOPS, and st1/sc1 are HDD-based, low-IOPS throughput volumes unsuitable for high-IOPS transactional workloads.

stem: Which S3 storage class is designed for data that is accessed less frequently but requires rapid, millisecond access when needed, and charges a per-GB retrieval fee?

choices.text: S3 Standard
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Intelligent-Tiering Archive Access tier

explanation: S3 Standard-IA offers the same millisecond access as S3 Standard but at a lower storage price with a retrieval fee, ideal for infrequently accessed data. S3 Standard has no retrieval fee, and the Glacier-based tiers require retrieval times ranging from minutes to hours, not milliseconds.

stem: A company wants to extend on-premises storage to the cloud so that frequently accessed data is cached locally for low-latency access while the full data set is durably stored in Amazon S3, presented to on-premises applications as an iSCSI block device. Which AWS solution meets this requirement?

choices.text: AWS DataSync
AWS Storage Gateway - Volume Gateway (cached volumes)
AWS Storage Gateway - File Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway - Tape Gateway

explanation: Volume Gateway in cached mode stores the full data set in S3 while keeping frequently accessed data cached locally, presenting volumes as iSCSI block devices to on-premises applications. File Gateway presents an NFS/SMB file interface rather than block/iSCSI, DataSync is a data transfer tool rather than a persistent hybrid storage interface, and Tape Gateway emulates a virtual tape library.

stem: A cluster-aware application requires multiple EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone to concurrently read and write to the same block storage volume. Which EBS feature enables this, and what is a key constraint the architect must plan for?

choices.text: EBS snapshots; the volume can only be attached after each snapshot completes
EBS Multi-Attach on io1/io2 volumes; the application must use a cluster-aware file system to manage concurrent writes
Elastic Volumes; it automatically prevents write conflicts
EFS mount targets; instances must be in different AZs

explanation: EBS Multi-Attach allows a single io1 or io2 volume to be attached to multiple instances in the same AZ, but because EBS does not arbitrate write ordering, the application or file system must be cluster-aware to prevent data corruption. Snapshots and Elastic Volumes address different concerns, and EFS is a separate file storage service unrelated to EBS Multi-Attach.

stem: An application uploads large video files (5 to 20 GB each) from users distributed globally directly to an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Users in Asia and Australia report slow, inconsistent upload speeds. Which combination of S3 features should the architect implement to improve upload performance without changing the bucket's Region?

choices.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and use multipart upload
Enable S3 Versioning and Cross-Region Replication
Switch to the S3 One Zone-IA storage class
Increase the size of the EC2 instance hosting the upload application

explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations over optimized AWS backbone network paths, and multipart upload parallelizes large file transfers, together improving throughput and consistency for geographically distant users. Versioning and replication address durability and disaster recovery rather than upload speed, and storage class or EC2 sizing changes do not address network transfer latency.

stem: A big data analytics workload running on hundreds of EC2 instances needs to read and write to a shared EFS file system with the highest possible aggregate throughput and operations per second, and can tolerate slightly higher per-operation latency. Which EFS performance mode should be selected?

choices.text: General Purpose
Max I/O
Bursting Throughput
Provisioned Throughput combined with General Purpose mode

explanation: Max I/O performance mode is optimized for highly parallelized workloads with thousands of connected instances, scaling to higher levels of aggregate throughput and IOPS at the cost of slightly higher per-operation latency. General Purpose mode has lower latency but a lower ceiling on aggregate operations, and Bursting/Provisioned Throughput are throughput modes, not performance modes.

stem: A database administrator anticipates that an application's storage needs will grow steadily over the next year and wants the ability to increase an EBS volume's size and change its volume type without detaching it or stopping the EC2 instance. Which EBS capability provides this?

choices.text: EBS Snapshots
Elastic Volumes
EBS Multi-Attach
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager

explanation: Elastic Volumes allow you to dynamically increase capacity, adjust performance, and change the volume type of an in-use EBS volume without detaching it or restarting the instance. Snapshots are point-in-time backups, Multi-Attach enables concurrent attachment, and Data Lifecycle Manager automates snapshot/AMI lifecycle policies, none of which resize volumes.

stem: An application on an EC2 instance backed by a 500 GB gp3 volume (at the default baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s) is experiencing high I/O wait times during peak load, and CloudWatch shows the VolumeQueueLength metric consistently elevated. The application cannot tolerate downtime for a volume swap. What is the MOST appropriate immediate remediation?

choices.text: Detach the volume and re-attach it to a larger instance
Increase the provisioned IOPS and throughput on the existing gp3 volume using Elastic Volumes
Take a snapshot, restore it to a new io2 volume, then swap volumes
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the instance

explanation: gp3 IOPS and throughput can be provisioned independently of size and modified live via Elastic Volumes without detaching the volume or stopping the instance, directly relieving the queue depth caused by hitting the baseline IOPS limit. Options A and C both require downtime or volume swaps the requirement rules out, and Transfer Acceleration is unrelated to EBS performance.

stem: A media company needs to run a nightly video transcoding job that processes thousands of files, with individual jobs sometimes running for several hours and requiring GPU instances. Which service is the BEST fit for orchestrating and running this workload?

choices.text: AWS Lambda
AWS Batch
Amazon API Gateway
AWS Step Functions alone, without a compute service

explanation: AWS Batch dynamically provisions the optimal compute resources, including GPU-enabled EC2 instances, based on job requirements and queue volume, and has no execution time limit, making it suited for long-running, resource-intensive batch jobs. Lambda has a 15-minute maximum execution timeout and no native GPU support, and Step Functions orchestrates workflows but still needs an underlying compute service to run the jobs.

stem: A genomics research application performs in-memory processing of very large datasets that must be held entirely in RAM, with only moderate CPU and network requirements. Which EC2 instance family is the MOST appropriate starting point?

choices.text: C-family (compute optimized)
R-family (memory optimized)
T-family (burstable general purpose)
I-family (storage optimized)

explanation: R-family instances provide a high ratio of memory to vCPU, making them ideal for workloads that process large in-memory datasets. C-family is optimized for compute-intensive tasks, T-family suits occasional CPU bursts rather than sustained memory needs, and I-family is optimized for high, sequential local NVMe storage I/O.

stem: An EC2 Auto Scaling group uses a target tracking policy on average CPU utilization, but CloudWatch metrics show the group repeatedly scaling out and then immediately scaling back in every few minutes, causing instability. What is the MOST likely cause and correct fix?

choices.text: The instance warm-up period configured in the target tracking policy is too short, so newly launched instances are counted in the aggregated metric before reaching steady state, causing premature scale-in; increase the warm-up period
The Auto Scaling group's maximum size is set too low; increase the maximum size
The launch template references an invalid AMI; update the AMI ID
The target tracking metric should be changed to network utilization instead of CPU

explanation: If the warm-up period is too short, the policy evaluates the metric before new instances have had time to take on load and stabilize, causing the aggregated metric to drop and triggering premature scale-in, which produces an oscillating pattern. A low maximum size would prevent scale-out rather than cause flapping, an invalid AMI would cause launch failures instead, and simply switching metrics does not fix the underlying timing issue.

stem: A company needs to run distributed Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs to process petabytes of data stored in Amazon S3, using a managed cluster that can scale nodes up and down based on workload. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?

choices.text: Amazon EMR
AWS Glue Studio visual jobs only
Amazon Redshift
AWS Batch

explanation: Amazon EMR is a managed big data platform for running distributed frameworks such as Apache Spark, Hadoop, Hive, and Presto at scale, with the ability to dynamically resize clusters. AWS Glue is primarily a serverless ETL service rather than a general-purpose managed cluster platform, Redshift is a data warehouse, and AWS Batch runs generic batch jobs rather than distributed big-data frameworks natively.

stem: A fleet of EC2 instances consumes messages from an SQS standard queue to perform image processing that takes an unpredictable amount of time, sometimes exceeding the queue's default visibility timeout. Workers report receiving and reprocessing messages that another worker is still handling. What should a worker do while it continues processing a message it has already received?

choices.text: Reduce the visibility timeout to 0 seconds
Call ChangeMessageVisibility to extend the timeout dynamically while processing continues
Switch to an SNS topic instead of SQS
Increase the number of consumers polling the queue
